Merge bitcoin/bitcoin#36439: test: poll more frequently in sync helpers and RPC connection wait

8898f832d9d86d5a6a8ad8719e1009c702bbf4bd test: poll more frequently in sync helpers and RPC connection wait (ViniciusCestarii)

Pull request description:

  Tested on  my x86-64 machine:

  - Wall time (-j=18): 110.8s to 96.4s (−13%)
  - Accumulated: 1715s to 1369s (−20%)

  Also compared the CI on my fork (time for test_runner.py runtime):

  - macOS native: [1287s](https://github.com/ViniciusCestarii/bitcoin/actions/runs/37308619216/job/111758264512#step:9:4745) to [1175s](https://github.com/ViniciusCestarii/bitcoin/actions/runs/37318654530/job/111791769239#step:9:4744) (-9%)
  - 32 bit ARM: [776s](https://github.com/ViniciusCestarii/bitcoin/actions/runs/37308619216/job/111758264778#step:10:6336) to [690s](https://github.com/ViniciusCestarii/bitcoin/actions/runs/37318654530/job/111791769348#step:10:5806) (-11%)
  - Windows native, VS: [1456s](https://github.com/ViniciusCestarii/bitcoin/actions/runs/37308619216/job/111758264639#step:14:1486) to [1252s](https://github.com/ViniciusCestarii/bitcoin/actions/runs/37318654530/job/111791768933#step:14:1486) (-14%)
  - previous releases: [930s](https://github.com/ViniciusCestarii/bitcoin/actions/runs/37308619216/job/111758264815#step:10:5510) to [786s](https://github.com/ViniciusCestarii/bitcoin/actions/runs/37318654530/job/111791769195#step:10:6016) (-15%)
  - No wallet: [614s](https://github.com/ViniciusCestarii/bitcoin/actions/runs/37308619216/job/111758264997#step:10:5421) to [572s](https://github.com/ViniciusCestarii/bitcoin/actions/runs/37318654530/job/111791769524#step:10:5813) (-7%)
  - Alpine (musl): [1958s](https://github.com/ViniciusCestarii/bitcoin/actions/runs/37308619216/job/111758265011#step:10:5041) to [1970s](https://github.com/ViniciusCestarii/bitcoin/actions/runs/37318654530/job/111791769871#step:10:5489) (+0.6%)

  Sanitizer jobs are left out because they vary too much between runs.

  Alpine (musl) uses --usecli, so more frequent poll creates a new bitcoin-cli process each time, making it not faster with these changes. Also tried locally with --usecli: from 2060s to 2051s accumulated.

commit.message:
Merge bitcoin/bitcoin#36535: policy: sum package weight in int64_t

faaabe4454c14537e9f23bd349d43d7233df14fe policy: sum package weight in int64_t (Ferdinando Ametrano)

Pull request description:

  `IsWellFormedPackage` sums the package weight with `std::accumulate` starting from a plain `0`, so the running total is an `int`. A package heavier than `INT_MAX` would wrap and could pass the `MAX_PACKAGE_WEIGHT` check. No package that large reaches this check today, since RPC request bodies are capped at 32 MiB and P2P messages at 4 MB, so this is defense in depth. It picks up the one-line fix from #35473, which was closed with an invitation to do so.

  I start the sum from `int64_t{0}`, as the vsize sum in `validation.cpp` already does. I did not add a test, since the one on #35473 was turned down. I checked the fix locally with a throwaway test that puts one transaction of 88M weight into a package 25 times: before the fix the package is rejected as `package-contains-duplicates`, after it as `package-too-large`.

commit.message:
policy: sum package weight in int64_t

std::accumulate keeps its running total in the type of its initial
value. IsWellFormedPackage passed a plain 0, so the package weight was
summed in an int, even though the lambda and the result are int64_t.
A package heavier than INT_MAX would wrap and could pass the
MAX_PACKAGE_WEIGHT check. No such package reaches this check today:
RPC request bodies and P2P messages are far smaller.

Start the sum from int64_t{0}, as the vsize sum in validation.cpp
already does.

Merge bitcoin/bitcoin#36446: test: remove some avoidable test waits

ce1d88b2632cc3950f47d8b191bdd74b806eb3ae test: avoid unused wallet test chains (will)
40619d068741ec609ddd3148f13234cbdc54161c bench: honor configured wallet epochs (will)
79bb94f09244ef5745d3c83a8839eec3fcbf2f74 test: cap expected IPC timeouts (will)
06cb869112da6bb1c43f938b2e5a9794f825ff92 test: shorten network limited negative wait (will)

Pull request description:

  A few of our longer-running tests have some unnecessary waits and timeouts in them. Reduce or replace them to shorten test times:

  - in `p2p_node_network_limited` replace the expected sync timeout with header/ping barriers and a bounded negative check. At CI timeout factor 40, saves roughly 195 seconds per transport.
  - in `interface_ipc_mining` cap three expected no-event waits at five seconds, saving roughly 105 seconds at factor 40 in CI.
  - in `WalletLoadingDescriptors` honor sanity mode’s single epoch, avoiding four unnecessary wallet unload/load cycles.
  - two wallet unit tests switch to `BasicTestingSetup` avoiding construction of two unused 100-block chains.

  The timeout changes alone save approximately eight minutes of accumulated test-worker time on CI jobs running both transports and IPC mining. Wall-clock savings depend on parallel scheduling, CPU etc.

Merge bitcoin/bitcoin#36469: refactor: deduplicate block validation state catcher

c9cccf6d68c682e533876b4450f5ad7044a79f10 refactor: deduplicate block validation state catcher (Enoch Azariah)

Pull request description:

  As mentioned in https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/34644#discussion_r2889315162 and https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35675#discussion_r360301816, the validation state catchers were defined in the block template manager, `submitblock` rpc and mining test helpers, even though they do the same thing.

  Moved this helper into `node/block_validation_state_catcher.h` and reuse it across all three callers. An optional validation state replaces the separate `found` flag where used, preserving each caller's registration and result handling

  Replaces #36389 with the same commit on a dedicated branch.
